problem.title:
Solo Projects Die

for Predictable Reasons

quotes.backend: “I wrote the backend. The UI is still three unstyled forms.”
quotes.idea: “I know what to build. I don't know what to build first.”
quotes.alone: “We started with four people. By week three, I was alone again.”

problem.summary: At work you own one layer and specialists cover the rest. On a side project, you're all of them at once. That's why the ambitious ones never ship.

howItWorks.title:
From Idea

to Shipped in One Cycle

define.title: Define the build
define.description: Describe what you're making, what's in scope, and how long the cycle runs. Two to twelve weeks. Fixed from day one.

roles.title: Open your roles
roles.description: Missing a designer? A backend dev? Open a slot for each one, with the skills and the weekly hours you expect.

team.title: Pick your team
team.description: People apply to a specific slot and tell you why they want in. You read, you choose. No algorithm decides for you.

ship.title: Ship and log it
ship.description: Work the cycle, close it out, and every member walks away with the project in their profile — role, dates, outcome.

features.title:
Built for Teams That

Only Exist for a While

scope.title:
Scope That Can't

Quietly Grow
scope.description: The scope is public before anyone joins. If you change it mid-cycle, everyone gets notified and gets a week to walk away without a mark on their profile. Ambition stays honest.

roles.title:
Roles, Not Vague

Invitations
roles.description: Every open seat names the skills, the direction, and the hours. Applicants know what they're signing up for, and you know what you're choosing between.

deadline.title: A Deadline That Actually Lands
deadline.description: Projects without an end date don't fail — they fade. Every Berth project runs a fixed cycle and closes with a real outcome: shipped, partly shipped, or abandoned. All three go in your profile, because the honest record is worth more than a graveyard of "in progress."

keyBenefit.title:
Goodbye Solo Burnout.

Hello Shipped Work.
keyBenefit.subtitle: Most people are both. Post one project, join another — nothing in Berth asks you to pick a side.

showcases.subtitle: Every project here ran a fixed cycle with a real team. No mockups, no demos.

free.question: Is Berth free?
free.answer: Yes, completely. No paid tiers, no limits on projects or applications.

equity.question: Do I give up equity or sign anything?
equity.answer: No. Berth has no contracts, no equity splits, and no ownership claims. It's a place to find people and run a cycle — the rest is between you and your team.

code.question: Who owns the code we write?
code.answer: You and your team do. Berth never touches your repository. Pick a license before the cycle starts and you'll save yourself an awkward conversation later.

unfinished.question: What if the project doesn't finish?
unfinished.answer: It still counts. Cycles close as shipped, partly shipped, or abandoned, and your profile records what you actually did. An unfinished project with a real team beats another half-read tutorial.

github.question: Do I need a GitHub account?
github.answer: No. Sign up with an email and a password. You can link GitHub or GitLab later if you want it on your profile.

concurrent.question: Can I join a project and run my own at the same time?
concurrent.answer: Yes. Up to three projects as an author and five as a member.
